takeaway: The macula, the centre of fine vision, is grossly over-represented in the visual cortex.

question.text: With regard to visual field pathways, which statement is true?

answer.text: The macula region is grossly over-represented in the visual cortex
answer.say: The answer is: the macula region is grossly over-represented in the visual cortex.

lines.say: This eye is the projector. Rods and cones in the retina turn light into electrical impulses.

lines.text: The macula is a tiny spot.
lines.say: The macula is a tiny spot on the retina, the centre of sharp vision.

lines.text: At the chiasm, nasal fibres cross.
lines.say: At the optic chiasm, the fibres cross only partly. Nasal fibres cross, while temporal fibres stay on the same side.

lines.text: But the macula fills the big screen.
lines.say: (laugh) But look at the screen. That tiny macula fills almost all of it.

lines.text: The visual cortex gives it the most space.
lines.say: The visual cortex gives the macula far more space than its size.

lines.text: Remember: the macula is grossly over-represented in the visual cortex.
lines.say: Remember: the macula is grossly over-represented in the visual cortex.
